declarations.name: Lemma L1. The canonical quotient tree and its fibre coordinates
declarations.scope: For a minimal degree-d quotient tuple with full-cycle product, deleting the parent-return edge of each quotient cycle gives a canonical tree. Root-normalized fibre charts uniquely make its tree transports identity; the remaining maps are common-fibre return permutations.

declarations.name: Theorem L2. A literal degree-reducing return-tuple bijection
declarations.scope: For each fixed literal quotient q of r factors, original minimal lifts with product P_(bd) are in literal bijection with M=(r-1)d+1 return factors on b letters, product P_b and total index b-1. Local cycle inflation ell*nu is the only original-passport constraint. Explicit reconstruction and product straightening recover every original permutation exactly.

declarations.name: Theorem L3. Exact transport and the quotient-stabilizer action
declarations.scope: Wreath-coordinate multiplication, original signed Hurwitz moves and return extraction give the exact coupled transport. Above one quotient braid component, original components are exactly the orbits of the quotient stabilizer on admissible lower-degree return tuples. Explicit finite Schreier loops generate that action; no full inner braid action is assumed.

declarations.name: Theorem L4. Decorated quotient components are sufficient for \(b=2,3\)
declarations.scope: For b=2 or3, decorated quotient braid components, recording every return partition at its quotient cycle, are sufficient component labels. The only literal fibre multiplicities are1 or3, and available full-twist root phases connect them. The cyclic stabilizer formula is bs/f and corresponding absolute orbit sizes agree. This does not extend to b4.

declarations.name: Theorem L5. Complete lifting over a free cyclic branch
declarations.scope: For any b>=2 and degree-d quotient passport, add one single b-cycle branch and replace all other quotient factors by b disjoint copies. In the union of original components preserving blocks of size b, there is exactly one component above each quotient component. Stabilizer image on the d marked blocks is exactly K; group C_b wr K, literal size d(s+1)L, deck order b and absolute size(s+1)L. Other original components lacking this block system are excluded explicitly.

declarations.name: Lemma L6. Monodromy containing a transposition
declarations.scope: Every transitive group containing a transposition is the full imprimitive wreath S_a wr K, with canonical blocks from the normal-closure support graph and normal subgroup S_a^e. This is independent of the chosen transposition. Its natural centralizer is trivial for a>=3 and diagonal C2 for a2. No genus assumption or component uniqueness follows.

declarations.name: Corollary L7. An infinite higher-index component catalogue
declarations.scope: The free cyclic-branch construction lifts the complete minimal index-two component catalogue in every b>=2. In degree7b, passport(2^(2b)1^(3b))^3 plus(b1^(6b)) has, in its block-size-b subdomain, two C_b-wr-A7 components of literal size4116/absolute588 and two C_b-wr-PSL3(2) components1372/196, each deck order b. In particular the two A7 lifts have the same standard embedded group but are distinct components. Generic connected-quotient sizes use L=binom(s,k)d^(s-1)(s-1)^m.

declarations.name: Theorem L8. The first nontrivial return-coupling obstruction
declarations.scope: The degree8 passport(4,2,2),(2,2,1^4) has full literal orbit sizes16,16,8 and exact groups576,576,64 with deck orders1,1,2. Both576 groups are the identical parity kernel H in S4 wr S2. In the all-transposition-return sector the quotient and full inner components are each unique, but the quotient-stabilizer action has two8-cycles, giving two glued components. Direct complete enumeration proves this finite sharpness result.

declarations.name: Proposition L9. A canonical divisor prevents decomposition overcounting
declarations.scope: For every imprimitive component choose the largest proper admissible block-count divisor d*. This invariant numerical choice partitions the imprimitive domain without overcounting nonunique decomposition chains. Quotient and fibre degrees are smaller than N; deleting quotient identities creates no new full-braid components. Complete primitive Sn/An classification plus known rigid/exceptional cases and the remaining return actions would therefore yield the full classification by induction. The latter inputs remain open.
